summary: Backend re-tested end-to-end after the register _id fix. 27/28 checks pass. Only remaining bug: POST /api/conversations/messages returns 500 due to the same ObjectId-leak pattern (motor mutates the dict in place after insert_one and FastAPI cannot serialize the resulting _id). All other flows work: auth (register/login/me/patch language), profiles+filters, likes with reciprocal match creating conversation, messages GET with 403 for non-participants, gifts 70/30 split with proper balance deltas, videocall coin deduction, date booking 400 (insufficient) and 400 (below-min), wallet returns coins/escrow/withdrawable/transactions, withdraw success + 400 for insufficient, Stripe checkout returns checkout_url+session_id, payments/status returns pending, upload PNG + download via /api/files/{path}, GET /dates returns outgoing+incoming.
passed: POST /api/gifts/send rose: cost=50, commission=15, net=35; sender coins 100->50; recipient withdrawable 0->35 (70/30 correct)
POST /api/dates/book coins=500 with only 40 coins -> 400 Insufficient coins
POST /api/upload PNG -> storage path + url returned
GET /api/dates -> {outgoing, incoming} (no error, escrow release path executes cleanly)

failed.issue: Returns 500 Internal Server Error. Same root cause as the earlier register bug: server.py:313 does `await db.messages.insert_one(msg)` then returns `msg` on line 315. Motor mutates `msg` in place and adds `_id: ObjectId(...)`, which FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize. Traceback confirmed in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log: `ValueError: [TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable")]`. GET messages still works because it uses projection {"_id":0}, so message persistence is fine — only the POST response fails. Impact: clients receive 500 even though the message is saved.
failed.evidence: curl POST /api/conversations/messages -> HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error'. Backend log: ValueError: [TypeError("'ObjectId' object is not iterable")]

action_items: Fix server.py POST /conversations/messages (line 307-315): strip _id before returning. Simplest patch — build the response dict without mutation, e.g. return `{k: v for k, v in msg.items() if k != '_id'}`, or insert a copy: `await db.messages.insert_one(dict(msg))`. Same defensive pattern should be applied wherever a dict is returned right after insert_one (audit /wallet/withdraw line 437 — currently uses `if k != '_id'` filter, which is fine).
After fix, retest only POST /api/conversations/messages; all other flows already verified green.
